files_created.purpose: Improved the existing standard-library text statistics tool: count_text() returns exactly the four integer keys under the single authoritative caliber (normalise one leading U+FEFF, CRLF then lone CR to LF, split on LF only, trailing LF opens no extra line, word regex [A-Za-z]+(?:[-'\u2019][A-Za-z]+)*), main(argv, stdin_text) keeps the two call scopes apart (explicit stdin_text returns only an exit code and touches no process stream; stdin_text None runs the CLI and writes exactly four '<key>: <value>' lines), every handled error (missing/unreadable/directory path, decode failure, unknown --encoding, more than one positional argument) exits 1 with an 'error: ' line and no traceback instead of argparse's 2, the redundant single-line forwarding helpers _normalize/_split_lines/_count_lines are gone so count_text and main call the real logic directly, and the dead 'if text is None' branch in main() was removed.

Unit tests for both contracts (grew 77 -> 81 tests): added a CRLF/lone-CR mixed input (AC-02/AC-14: 'a\r\nb\rc' = 5/3/3/3), a test that a programmatic empty-text call never touches or blocks on sys.stdin (AC-13, via a stdin whose read() raises), a programmatic unknown-encoding error test (AC-19), an AST test that nothing but the __main__ guard calls main() and that no wrapper named run/_main exists (AC-20), plus strengthened the U+2019 readability test (AC-21) and the one-line-forwarder test (BC-21) to walk the module AST instead of doing substring checks.

Documentation kept in step with this round's authority: the stale 'unreachable AC-05 value 6 / awaiting human ruling' section was replaced by a worked example fixing "  \r\n \r\n" at char_count 5 (never 6) with a field-by-field basis table and the statement that run 5's recorded conflict is dissolved; added a char-count comparison table (BC-02/03/08) and a priority note that AC-05 is 5. All copy-paste examples still agree with sample_input.txt and with AC-01..AC-14.
Evidence artifact for this coding stage: envelope (run_id/agent/stage/generated_at) plus the exact result object returned to the pipeline.

result.implementation_summary: No behavioural change was needed: a re-run of my independent audit over AC-01..AC-20 (line boundaries, normalisation order, BOM handling, char/line/non-empty/word calibers, both call scopes, all five error paths, --help, standard-library-only imports, guard shape, README example consistency) reported AUDIT FAILURES: 0 both before and after my edits, so the four statistics and the CLI output were already correct. What I fixed were the surviving defects the requirement named: (1) README still described the previous round's AC-05 char_count 6 as an unreachable value awaiting a human ruling, contradicted by this round's authoritative 5 -- rewritten with a worked example and a char-count table; (2) text_stats.py carried a dead branch in main() (an 'if text is None' check after the path/stdin branches that no execution path could reach) -- main() was restructured into path-branch / programmatic-branch / stdin-branch with a single 'if not programmatic' write, preserving the rule that a programmatic call still reports an unreadable PATH or a bad --encoding as an error while writing nothing; (3) the module docstring now states the programmatic-call contract and the AC-05 figure explicitly. Tests were extended from 77 to 81 to cover AC-02/AC-13/AC-19/AC-20 directly and the AC-21/BC-21 checks were made real AST checks instead of substring probes (one self-inflicted failure along the way: 'assertNotIn("_main", source)' matched the "__main__" guard, fixed by inspecting parsed top-level function names). No bare U+2019 character exists anywhere in the delivery directory, so AC-21 already held. Dependencies remain Python standard library only and no dependency manifest was added.
